analysis.title: ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON): Solid quarter and guidance, with automotive headwinds offsetting datacenter strength
key_insights: GS expects ON stock to be range bound after a 3Q26 print where revenue and EPS were in line with the Street and 4Q guidance came in just above.

3Q26 revenue was $1.72 bn, in line with GS at $1.72 bn and the Street (Visible Alpha) at $1.71 bn. Adjusted gross margin was 41.2% vs 41.1% for GS and the Street. EPS was $0.90 vs GS $0.90 and Street $0.88.

By segment, Automotive revenue of $777 mn missed GS ($820 mn) and the Street ($809 mn). Industrial revenue of $467 mn beat GS ($423 mn) and the Street ($426 mn). Datacenter/Other revenue of $479 mn was in line with GS ($477 mn) and the Street ($473 mn).
ON disclosed AI Data Center revenue for the first time, at $180 mn in 3Q. Management expects $620 mn of AI datacenter sales in 2026 vs $250 mn in 2025.

ON agreed to acquire Ferric, a private maker of integrated voltage regulator power solutions for AI infrastructure, for $600 mn in cash plus up to $175 mn of contingent consideration. Closing is expected by the end of 2026.
With the Ferric deal, management raised its 2030 datacenter revenue forecast to $3 bn from $2.5 bn and expects datacenter revenue to grow in the mid-teens percent q/q in 4Q.

Automotive revenue fell 1% q/q as China EV strength was offset by normal seasonality in Europe. Supply constraints are limiting the segment, and ON is supporting end demand but not restocking or buffer inventory requests. Management guided automotive down high single digits q/q in 4Q, with normalization in 1Q27.

Fab utilization rose to 83% in 3Q and is guided flat to up in 4Q. Management guided continued gross margin improvement through 2027, and still sees each 1% of utilization adding about 25-30bps of gross margin. Pricing actions to offset high input costs should be recognized over the coming quarters.
4Q26 guidance midpoint: revenue $1.77 bn (GS $1.79 bn, Street $1.74 bn), gross margin 42.5% (GS 42.5%, Street 42.1%), adjusted EPS $0.95-$1.07 with a $1.01 midpoint (GS $1.02, Street $0.95).

GS cut its 12-month target to $85 from $95, using an 18x P/E (down from 20x on lower peer multiples) on unchanged normalized EPS of $4.75. Rating stays Neutral because of automotive exposure, SiC and image sensor headwinds, and residual pricing pressure.
GS sees a neutral read-through for the analog group since most peers have already reported, with ADI (Buy) the most direct read-across because of its automotive exposure.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $85 from $95 on an 18x P/E (from 20x) applied to unchanged normalized EPS of $4.75. Neutral because of automotive exposure and SiC and image sensor headwinds.
GS expects the most direct read-across from ON's results to fall on ADI because of its relatively high automotive exposure.

sector_views.rationale: GS keeps a constructive stance on the analog sector but is Neutral on ON given its automotive exposure and pricing headwinds in parts of its portfolio.

earnings_insights: ON reported 3Q26 revenue of $1.72 bn (reported 11/2 after close), in line with GS $1.72 bn and Street (Visible Alpha) consensus $1.71 bn. The report's Exhibit 1 shows Street total revenue at $1,706 mn.
ON 3Q26 EPS (incl. SBC) was $0.90 reported vs GS $0.90 and Street consensus $0.88. Gross margin (excl. SBC) was 41.2% vs 41.1% for GS and the Street.
3Q26 revenue grew 29.2% q/q and 34.6% y/y per Exhibit 1.

4Q26 guidance: revenue $1.715-$1.815 bn (midpoint $1.765 bn) vs GS estimate $1.79 bn and Street $1.74 bn. Adjusted EPS guidance $0.95-$1.07 (midpoint $1.01) vs GS estimate $1.02 and Street consensus $0.95. Gross margin guidance midpoint 42.5% vs Street 42.1%.
4Q26 end-market guidance: Automotive down high single digits q/q, Industrial up low double digits q/q, AI Datacenter up mid-teens q/q, Other up high teens q/q.

GS estimates (new vs old): 2026E revenue $6,623 mn (old $6,628 mn), EPS $3.30 (unchanged). 2027E revenue $7,533 mn (old $7,551 mn), EPS $4.59 (unchanged). 2028E revenue $8,251 mn (old $8,163 mn), EPS $5.69 (old $5.60).

GS cut its Automotive revenue estimates by 5% for 2026E, 10% for 2027E and 9% for 2028E, and raised Industrial by 6%, 5% and 1%. It models AI Datacenter revenue of $620 mn in 2026E, $1,203 mn in 2027E and $1,625 mn in 2028E.
risk_factors: Demand weakness, particularly in the Automotive end market, could drive downside.
Gross margin execution and the timing of self-help initiatives could drive earnings upside or downside.
Supply chain constraints are driving near-term softness in automotive.
Residual pricing headwinds in parts of the portfolio, plus headwinds in the SiC and image sensor businesses.
